passages.scripture: As a fellow elder, a witness of Christ’s sufferings, and a partaker of the glory to be revealed, I appeal to the elders among you: Be shepherds of God’s flock that is among you, watching over them not out of compulsion, but because it is God’s will; not out of greed, but out of eagerness; not lording it over those entrusted to you, but being examples to the flock.

lines.text: An elder is a leader who shepherds God's people.
Peter himself is an elder.
So Peter writes to his fellow elders.
Peter saw Christ's sufferings with his own eyes.
Peter also saw Christ's glory, when Jesus was transfigured on the mountain.
And Peter will share in the glory that God will soon reveal.
So Peter appeals to the elders among you:
Shepherd God's flock — the people God has placed in your care.
Watch over the flock, but never because you feel forced.
Shepherd willingly instead, because this is what God wants.
Do not shepherd the flock just to make money.
Shepherd eagerly, glad to serve God's people.
Do not lord it over those entrusted to you.
Do not rule them like a harsh master, forceful and controlling.
Instead, lead by being an example the flock can follow.

passages.scripture: And when the Chief Shepherd appears, you will receive the crown of glory that will never fade away.

lines.text: Jesus Christ is the Chief Shepherd over all shepherds who shepherd His people.
One day Jesus will appear.
When He appears, you will receive the crown of glory.
This crown will never fade away.

passages.scripture: Young men, in the same way, submit yourselves to your elders. And all of you, clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, because, “God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”

lines.text: In the same way, you who are younger must submit to your elders.
God says that He opposes the proud.
But He gives grace to the humble.
So, all of you, clothe yourselves with humility toward one another.
And receive the grace of God.

passages.scripture: Humble yourselves, therefore, under God’s mighty hand, so that in due time He may exalt you.

lines.text: God's mighty hand means His great power over all things.
So humble yourselves under God's mighty hand.
Then, at the right time, God will exalt you.
When God exalts you, He will bless you with good far beyond anything you can imagine.

passages.scripture: Cast all your anxiety on Him, because He cares for you.

lines.text: God cares about you, and wants the very best for your life.
So throw your worries onto God — He knows whether or not you really need what you're worried about.
And even if you do not have it, God's grace is enough to strengthen you to endure every difficulty.

passages.scripture: Be sober-minded and alert. Your adversary the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour.

lines.text: The devil is your enemy, and he fights against you.
He is looking for someone to swallow up.
He prowls around like a roaring lion.
So keep a clear head, and stay alert.

passages.scripture: Resist him, standing firm in your faith and in the knowledge that your brothers throughout the world are undergoing the same kinds of suffering.

lines.text: Resist the devil.
Stand firm in your faith.
You have brothers and sisters in Christ all over the world.
And these believers are going through the same suffering as you.
Stand firm, knowing this.

passages.scripture: And after you have suffered for a little while, the God of all grace, who has called you to His eternal glory in Christ, will Himself restore you, secure you, strengthen you, and establish you.

lines.text: You will suffer for only a little while.
God is full of all grace.
God has called you to His eternal glory in Christ.
God Himself will restore you.
God will steady you.
God will strengthen you.
God will set you on a firm foundation.

passages.scripture: Through Silvanus, whom I regard as a faithful brother, I have written to you briefly, encouraging you and testifying that this is the true grace of God. Stand firm in it.

lines.text: Peter sent this letter through a man named Silvanus.
Peter considers Silvanus a faithful brother.
Peter has written to you in just a few words.
Peter wrote to encourage you.
Peter also wrote to testify that this is the grace of God.
This grace of God is true.
So stand firm in this grace of God.

passages.scripture: To Him be the power forever and ever. Amen.

lines.text: All power belongs to God.
God — the Creator — will reign over all creation forever and ever.
Amen.

passages.scripture: The church in Babylon, chosen together with you, sends you greetings, as does my son Mark.

lines.text: God has chosen you.
And God has chosen the church in Babylon.
This church sends you greetings.
And Mark, Peter's son, also greets you.

passages.scripture: Greet one another with a kiss of love. Peace to all of you who are in Christ.

lines.text: Greet one another.
Greet with a kiss of love.
Peace to all of you.
This peace is for everyone who is in Christ.
